analysis.title: International Market Intelligence - Morning Briefing (November 13, 2026)
key_insights: Tone is cautious into the weekend: APAC pared gains and US/EU futures trimmed losses into the open. Themes are the fragility of the post-midterm geopolitical narrative, the NVDA leadership change and next week's catalysts.
NVDA CEO resignation fallout was relatively contained. NVDA staged a notable intraday recovery with retail a key support (+10z of NVDA buying yesterday).

Trump's comments of 'no need for Iran deal' show the fragility of the geopolitical narrative the market priced in after the midterms. The selloff was clearest across global rates, a second knee-jerk reaction after this week's hot US CPI and hawkish Fed speak.
Sustainability of the broadening trade depends on an improving geopolitical landscape, with the EU a clear beneficiary so far. Flows continue to improve but so do strikes.
EU outperformed the US yesterday, but under the hood the move looked risk-off: recession L/S led in the US and the tape favored buying healthcare and staples in EMEA.

The US TMT trader flags financing as the key risk with Jensen gone. Neoclouds were the worst performing basket across the AI themes yesterday. The leadership change is the clear bear scenario, but a lot of negativity was already priced in and clarity is supportive.

UK GDP rose 0.7% in 3Q (3% annualized) on strong domestic final demand, with September up 0.2% m/m. JPM revises 4Q GDP up from 1.0% to 1.5% annualized and 1Q GDP down from 1.6% to 1.0% annualized because energy bills are set to rise sharply in 1Q.

Euro area employment growth has weakened despite resilient activity, and the periphery's job gains offsetting core losses have narrowed. JPM expects recovery to 0.3% annualized in 4Q26 and about 0.5% from 1Q27, which requires a hiring recovery in core countries.

Metro Bank announced a strategic review including a formal sale process, continuing consolidation among UK challenger banks. JPM expects large UK banks to show limited appetite for the business and sees asset/liability sales as unlikely outside a break-up (deposits of £13bn including c£6bn current accounts).

Market Intelligence is tactically bullish on global equities, with a regional preference of long US and Asia (Japan, South Korea, Taiwan) versus EU. The US is overheating, Europe is recovering from stagflation, and Asia has pockets of both.
The broadening trade can return more clearly in US than EU. Europe earnings fundamentals are good and positioning gives a buy signal, but stability in EGB spreads is needed for conviction in EU.

Positioning Intelligence: Multi-Strat de-grossing was the largest 20-day event since Covid, but long-short spreads improved this week. When Multi-Strat 20-day gross flows first fell below the 5th percentile (Oct 27), alpha was higher over the next 20 days in 9 of 10 cases.

HF net leverage fell about 4% over the past week to near 12-month lows. Eq L/S net leverage is at a three-year low. Global momentum exposure is near three-year lows and close to neutral. Semis remained the most net-sold US theme.
In Europe, HF short covering reached an extreme 3z level, last seen in late 2022. North America and Japan saw net selling and EMEA and China/HK saw net buying. Broad capitulation has not yet shown.

Next week catalysts: ASEAN Summit, COP31, China IP and FAI, EU foreign and defense ministers meeting, UK PM Burnham's foreign policy speech, UK labour data and CPI, US IP, Retail Sales and FOMC minutes, MSFT Ignite, BABA and NVDA earnings, EU-UK summit.

risk_factors: Financing risk for NVDA and neoclouds with the CEO departure.
Fragile geopolitical narrative on Iran after the midterms.
Instability in EGB spreads could hold back the EU broadening.
Hot US CPI and hawkish Fed speak pressuring global rates.
Further HF de-grossing, with the path described as murky and midterm-year precedent showing a December market sell-off.
vol_and_positioning: Multi-Strat 20-day de-grossing was the largest since Covid. 5-day alpha is close to flat after positive Tuesday and Thursday and a weak Wednesday.

After Multi-Strat 20-day gross flows fell below the 5th percentile, alpha was higher over the next 20 days in 9 of 10 cases. Gross flows typically recovered after about 10 days. The main exception was post-Covid.

US HF de-grossing is below its seasonal average. Past midterm years most resemble 2022, when de-grossing continued into mid-month and gross flows recovered in December alongside a market sell-off with substantial short additions.

In the past five years HFs rebounded over the following 5 and 10 days in all eight comparable events where 5- and 20-day net returns fell below -2z. Late Feb 2020 and late Oct 2018 saw further losses.
HF net leverage fell about 4% in a week to near 12-month lows. Eq L/S net leverage is at a three-year low and All Strategy net leverage is near the 40th percentile.

Global momentum exposure is near three-year lows. APAC momentum has fallen quickly. Semis are the most net-sold US theme, back near early-2026 positioning. Software flows are neutral. Defensives ex-Healthcare have begun to rebound.
geopolitical: Trump's comments of 'no need for Iran deal' undermined the geopolitical narrative priced in after the midterms.
US Congress returns after the Democrats' midterm win.
US-mediated talks between Russia and Ukraine on 10/11.
Flows into the EU improve as strikes also rise.
G7 foreign ministers met in Paris, UN COP31 held.
EU-UK summit next week with the post-Brexit relationship in focus.
